COBRApy · metabolic knockout analysis

NotebookTaskAttemptPipelineValidation

COBRApy · simulating gene and reaction deletions

The tool-repository notebook studies growth effects of metabolic gene and reaction knockouts in curated E. coli models. These models are reconstructions, not measured flux data. Pinned source notebook.

Source cells below; saved notebook outputs are not shown as fresh results.

Actual notebook JSON

 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Simulating Deletions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import pandas\n",
    "from time import time\n",
    "\n",
    "from cobra.io import load_model\n",
    "from cobra.flux_analysis import (\n",
    "    single_gene_deletion, single_reaction_deletion, double_gene_deletion,\n",
    "    double_reaction_deletion)\n",
    "\n",
    "cobra_model = load_model(\"textbook\")\n",
    "ecoli_model = load_model(\"iJO1366\")"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Knocking out single genes and reactions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "A commonly asked question when analyzing metabolic models is what will happen if a certain reaction was not allowed to have any flux at all. This can tested using cobrapy by"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "metadata": {
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "complete model:  <Solution 0.874 at 0x7fd813bf3390>\n",
      "pfk knocked out:  <Solution 0.704 at 0x7fd813bf31d0>\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())\n",
    "with cobra_model:\n",
    "    cobra_model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()\n",
    "    print('pfk knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "For evaluating genetic manipulation strategies, it is more interesting to examine what happens if given genes are knocked out as doing so can affect no reactions in case of redundancy, or more reactions if gene when is participating in more than one reaction."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "complete model:  <Solution 0.874 at 0x7fd813bf3c18>\n",
      "pfkA knocked out:  <Solution 0.874 at 0x7fd813bf35c0>\n",
      "pfkB knocked out:  <Solution 0.704 at 0x7fd813bf3588>\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())\n",
    "with cobra_model:\n",
    "    cobra_model.genes.b1723.knock_out()\n",
    "    print('pfkA knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())\n",
    "    cobra_model.genes.b3916.knock_out()\n",
    "    print('pfkB knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Single Deletions"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

   ]

   "cell_type": "code",

    "deletion_results = single_gene_deletion(cobra_model)"

# # Simulating Deletions

import pandas
from time import time

from cobra.io import load_model
from cobra.flux_analysis import (
    single_gene_deletion, single_reaction_deletion, double_gene_deletion,
    double_reaction_deletion)

cobra_model = load_model("textbook")
ecoli_model = load_model("iJO1366")

# ## Knocking out single genes and reactions

# A commonly asked question when analyzing metabolic models is what will happen if a certain reaction was not allowed to have any flux at all. This can tested using cobrapy by

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()
    print('pfk knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# For evaluating genetic manipulation strategies, it is more interesting to examine what happens if given genes are knocked out as doing so can affect no reactions in case of redundancy, or more reactions if gene when is participating in more than one reaction.

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.genes.b1723.knock_out()
    print('pfkA knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())
    cobra_model.genes.b3916.knock_out()
    print('pfkB knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# ## Single Deletions

# Perform all single gene deletions on a model

deletion_results = single_gene_deletion(cobra_model)

# These can also be done for only a subset of genes

single_gene_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[:20])

# This can also be done for reactions

single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[:20])

# ## Double Deletions

# Double deletions run in a similar way.

double_gene_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[-5:]).round(4)

# By default, the double deletion function will automatically use multiprocessing, splitting the task over up to 4 cores if they are available. The number of cores can be manually specified as well. Setting use of a single core will disable use of the multiprocessing library, which often aids debugging.

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=2)
t1 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 2 cores" % t1)

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=1)
t2 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 1 core" % t2)

print("Speedup of %.2fx" % (t2 / t1))

# Double deletions can also be run for reactions.

double_reaction_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[2:7]).round(4)

# ## Accessing individual deletion results
#
# Note that the indices for deletions are python [set](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/stdtypes.html#set-types-set-frozenset) objects. This is the appropriate type since the order of deletions does not matter. Deleting reaction 1 and reaction 2 will have the same effect as deleting reaction 2 and reaction 1. 
#
# To make it easier to access results all DataFrames returned by COBRAPpy deletion functions have a `knockout` indexer that makes that a bit simpler. Each entry in the indexer is treated as a single deletion entry. So you need to pass sets for double deletions.

single = single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)
double = double_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)

print(single.knockout["ATPM"])
print(double.knockout[{"ATPM", "TKT1"}])

# This can be used to get several deletions at once and will also work for Reaction or Gene objects (depending on what you deleted) directly.

atpm = cobra_model.reactions.ATPM
tkt1 = cobra_model.reactions.TKT1
pfk = cobra_model.reactions.PFK

print(single.knockout[atpm, tkt1, pfk])
print(double.knockout[{atpm, tkt1}, {atpm, pfk}, {atpm}])

Growth effects of gene and reaction knockouts in E. coli

The published solver question is below. Reference answers and grading code are separate from solver inputs.

Solver question

autonomous-runs/226/explorer-evidence/native/tasks/autonomous-panel-226/instruction.md

Growth effects of gene and reaction knockouts in the E. coli core metabolic model

Objective

You are given the curated "textbook" E. coli core metabolic model (BiGG id e_coli_core) as an SBML file. Using flux balance analysis (FBA), determine how every possible single-gene deletion, every single-reaction deletion, every pairwise reaction deletion, and four specific knockout scenarios that illustrate gene-level redundancy for phosphofructokinase affect the maximal achievable growth.

By "growth" we mean the optimal value of the model's biomass objective (the raw LP objective value; no rounding, clamping or sign correction). For every knockout scenario, report that optimum together with the status reported by the LP solve (e.g. optimal or infeasible).

Supplied input

  • inputs/e_coli_core.xml — the E. coli core metabolic model in SBML format, including its biomass objective reaction and gene–protein–reaction (GPR) associations. Use the model exactly as supplied; do not modify it, its medium, bounds or objective.

Knockout semantics

  • Reaction knockout: the reaction carries no flux; its flux is constrained to zero in both directions.
  • Gene knockout: a reaction is disabled only if its GPR rule evaluates to false once the knocked-out gene(s) are removed. If a reaction has a remaining functional isozyme gene (an OR in the GPR), the reaction still carries flux; a gene whose removal disables no reaction therefore has no growth effect even though the gene is knocked out.

Required outputs

Produce four CSV files, all with the columns knockouts,growth,status:

  • knockouts: the identifier(s) of the knocked-out entity, exactly as defined in the supplied model. For a knockout of multiple entities, the ids are sorted lexicographically and joined with ; (e.g. b1723;b3916, Biomass_Ecoli_core;LDH_D); a single-entity knockout uses just that entity's id.
  • growth: the optimal objective value of the LP after the knockout, as reported by the solver at full double precision, with no rounding, clamping or sign correction. Tiny negative values of magnitude around 1e-14 that arise from solver noise are expected and must be reported as-is. Leave this field empty when the knockout makes the problem infeasible.
  • status: the LP solve status string, e.g. optimal or infeasible.

1. single_gene_deletions.csv

One row for every gene defined in the supplied model (137 genes), including genes whose deletion disables no reaction.

2. single_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for every reaction defined in the supplied model (95 reactions, including boundary/exchange reactions).

3. double_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for each distinct knockout set {r_i, r_j} obtained by pairing every reaction in the model with every reaction in the model and reducing each ordered pair to an unordered set; the i = j cases contribute the single-reaction sets {r_i}. This yields the 95 singleton sets plus all C(95,2) = 4465 pairs, i.e. 4560 rows. Do not apply gene-level GPR logic here — both reactions are knocked out directly.

4. pfk_knockout_optima.csv

Exactly four rows, with the same column convention and an empty knockouts field for the no-knockout row:

  • (empty) — the unmodified (wild-type) model, no knockout;
  • PFK — the PFK reaction knocked out;
  • b1723 — gene b1723 (pfkA) knocked out;
  • b1723;b3916 — genes b1723 (pfkA) and b3916 (pfkB) knocked out simultaneously.

These quantify isozyme redundancy: the isozyme pfkB can compensate for a pfkA deletion, but not when both genes are removed.

Conventions

  • Row order in every file carries no scientific meaning; any row ordering is acceptable.
  • Growth is reported in the model's native biomass-objective units (the raw LP objective value).
  • Use the knockout populations exactly as defined above; do not skip entities that have no reaction associations or no growth effect.
  • Do not round any value (growth is written at full double precision).

Environment and resources

CPU only (up to 4 cores), 8 GiB RAM, no network access. Your program must complete within 600 seconds. Any software stack that satisfies the definitions above is acceptable; the results, not the tool, are what is compared.

Exact acceptance criteria (including numerical tolerances appropriate for LP-solver variation) are finalized separately during validation before the contract takes effect; produce results faithful to the definitions above.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules for the knockout-FBA outputs

Files compared. Exactly the four declared output files, each read as a comma-delimited UTF-8 CSV at its declared path relative to the supplied output root (no fallback directories, no extra outputs/ layer): single_gene_deletions.csv, single_reaction_deletions.csv, double_reaction_deletions.csv, pfk_knockout_optima.csv.

CSV syntax. Each file must carry exactly the header knockouts,growth,status and every data row must have exactly three fields (quoted empty fields and decimal values following standard CSV quoting are ordinary data; blank records are not permitted). Values must be plain decimal numbers in a standard fixed or scientific notation; hexadecimal, inf, nan or other nonfinite/invalid numerics fail. The growth field must be empty exactly when the solve is not optimal; for optimal rows it must contain a finite number.

Row alignment and ordering. Comparison is by the knockouts key, not by file position: any row order is acceptable. Each knockout label must appear exactly once; duplicate labels fail. Labels for multi-entity knockouts are the lexicographically sorted ids joined with ;; single-entity knockouts use the bare id. The empty wild-type row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv uses an empty knockouts field.

Coverage (input-grounded). The knockout population is derived from the supplied model e_coli_core.xml, not from the reference file: single_gene_deletions.csv must contain exactly one row per gene defined in the model; single_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per reaction defined in the model (including boundary/exchange reactions); double_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per single-reaction set and per unordered reaction pair (the 95 singletons plus all C(95,2) pairs, i.e. 4560 rows); pfk_knockout_optima.csv exactly the four rows "", PFK, b1723, b1723;b3916. Missing rows, extra rows or a different population fail.

Status comparison. The status string is compared exactly (e.g. optimal, infeasible); any status text that differs from the reference status for that knockout fails.

Numeric comparison. For each row with reference growth r and submission growth s, acceptance requires |s - r| <= max(1e-9 * max(|r|, |s|), 1e-11). The reference value is part of the denominator convention (the larger of the two magnitudes). This bound covers ordinary double-precision serialization and cross-solver variation, including the tiny (below ~5e-13 in magnitude) near-zero optima whose sign or exact zero-vs-noise value is solver-dependent; it does not license rounding to fewer significant digits, since genuine optimum differences between distinct knockout sets in this model are separated from that noise by several orders of magnitude. A growth value must not be clamped, sign-corrected or rounded to a coarser precision than that bound permits. An infeasible solve must be reported with an empty growth field, not zero.

Cross-file consistency. The following relations between the submitted files are enforced with the same tolerance: each single-reaction set row of double_reaction_deletions.csv must agree with the corresponding row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the PFK row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the PFK row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the b1723 gene row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv; the wild-type row must agree in growth with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv (isozyme pfkB compensates pfkA removal); and the b1723;b3916 row must agree with the PFK reaction-knockout rows (removing both PFK genes disables exactly the PFK reaction, which the supplied model's GPR associations define via b1723 and b3916 on PFK only).

No software stack is prescribed; any implementation producing these values is acceptable, and agreement of the alternative stacks used during validation is demonstrated, not assumed for others.

Task directories

Read the supplied inputs from /workspace/inputs/. Write all required output files under /workspace/outputs/, using the relative filenames specified above. The working directory is /workspace. Aliases /inputs/ and /outputs/ refer to these same directories.

Deterministic grader

autonomous-runs/226/explorer-evidence/grading/grade.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deterministic grader for E. coli core knockout FBA outputs.

Usage:
    python grade.py --reference-dir PATH --submission-dir PATH --report PATH

Compares four CSV artifacts (knockouts,growth,status) row-by-row after keying
on the knockouts label. Populations are derived from the trusted task input
(BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR/e_coli_core.xml), never from the submission.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

FBC = "{http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/fbc/version2}"
CORE = "{http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/core}"

GENE_FILE = "single_gene_deletions.csv"
REACTION_FILE = "single_reaction_deletions.csv"
DOUBLE_FILE = "double_reaction_deletions.csv"
PFK_FILE = "pfk_knockout_optima.csv"

PFK_LABELS = ["", "PFK", "b1723", ";".join(sorted(("b1723", "b3916")))]
HEADER = ["knockouts", "growth", "status"]

REL_TOL = 1e-9
ABS_TOL = 1e-11

ALL_FILES = [DOUBLE_FILE, GENE_FILE, PFK_FILE, REACTION_FILE]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- table syntax

def _read_table(path):
    """Read a comma-delimited table; return (header, rows) or raise."""
    try:
        from biotasks_table_io import read_delimited_table  # type: ignore
    except ImportError:
        read_delimited_table = None
    if read_delimited_table is not None:
        return read_delimited_table(path)
    records = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        for row in csv.reader(stream, delimiter=",", strict=True):
            if not row:
                raise ValueError("empty CSV record")
            records.append(row)
    if not records:
        raise ValueError("table has no header")
    header, rows = records[0], records[1:]
    if any(len(row) != len(header) for row in rows):
        raise ValueError("inconsistent row widths")
    return header, rows


def _load(path):
    """Return (table dict, None) or (None, error message)."""
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return None, "file not found: %s" % path
    try:
        header, rows = _read_table(path)
    except Exception as exc:  # malformed syntax is a failed check, not a crash
        return None, "unreadable or malformed CSV (%s): %s" % (path, exc)
    if header != HEADER:
        return None, "header is %r, expected %r" % (header, HEADER)
    if len(set(header)) != len(header):
        return None, "duplicate header names"
    table = {}
    for row in rows:
        key = row[0]
        if key in table:
            return None, "duplicate knockouts entry: %r" % key
        table[key] = (row[1], row[2])
    return table, None


# ------------------------------------------------------------ model population

def _model_population(trusted_dir):
    """Gene and reaction id populations from the trusted SBML input."""
    path = os.path.join(trusted_dir, "e_coli_core.xml")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise ValueError("trusted input model not found at %s" % path)
    root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    genes = []
    for element in root.iter(FBC + "geneProduct"):
        label = element.get(FBC + "label")
        identifier = element.get(FBC + "id")
        if not label or not identifier or not identifier.startswith("G_"):
            raise ValueError("geneProduct without usable label/id")
        if identifier[2:] != label:
            raise ValueError("geneProduct id/label mismatch: %s" % identifier)
        genes.append(label)
    reactions = []
    for element in root.iter(CORE + "reaction"):
        rid = element.get("id")
        if not rid or not rid.startswith("R_"):
            raise ValueError("reaction without usable id")
        reactions.append(rid[2:])
    if not genes or not reactions:
        raise ValueError("model population empty; unexpected SBML layout")
    if len(set(genes)) != len(genes) or len(set(reactions)) != len(reactions):
        raise ValueError("model population contains duplicate identifiers")
    return genes, reactions


def _double_population(reactions):
    keys = set(reactions)
    ordered = sorted(reactions)
    for i in range(len(ordered)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ordered)):
            keys.add(";".join(sorted((ordered[i], ordered[j]))))
    return keys


# ------------------------------------------------------------- value handling

def _parse_growth(cell):
    """Return (value, error). value is None for an empty cell."""
    if cell == "":
        return None, None
    try:
        value = float(cell)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None, "not a decimal number: %r" % cell
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        return None, "nonfinite value: %r" % cell
    return value, None


def _close(a, b):
    return abs(a - b) <= max(REL_TOL * max(abs(a), abs(b)), ABS_TOL)


def _compare(ref, sub):
    """Row-wise comparison keyed on knockouts. Returns list of problem strings."""
    problems = []
    for key in sorted(ref):
        ref_growth, ref_status = ref[key]
        sub_growth, sub_status = sub[key]
        if sub_status != ref_status:
            problems.append("%s: status %r != reference %r" % (key, sub_status, ref_status))
            continue
        if sub_status == "optimal":
            value, err = _parse_growth(sub_growth)
            if err is not None or value is None:
                problems.append("%s: growth %r is %s" % (key, sub_growth, err or "empty"))
                continue
            ref_value, ref_err = _parse_growth(ref_growth)
            if ref_err is not None or ref_value is None:
                problems.append("%s: reference growth unreadable" % key)
                continue
            if not _close(ref_value, value):
                problems.append(
                    "%s: growth %.17g differs from reference %.17g" % (key, value, ref_value)
                )
        else:
            if sub_growth != "":
                problems.append(
                    "%s: non-optimal status %r must have an empty growth field"
                    % (key, sub_status)
                )
    return problems


def _summary(problems, limit=5):
    if not problems:
        return "all rows match"
    shown = "; ".join(problems[:limit])
    more = "" if len(problems) <= limit else " (+%d more)" % (len(problems) - limit)
    return "%d row problems: %s%s" % (len(problems), shown, more)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- checks

CHECKS = [
    ("structure_single_gene_table", "structural", [GENE_FILE]),
    ("structure_single_reaction_table", "structural", [REACTION_FILE]),
    ("structure_double_reaction_table", "structural", [DOUBLE_FILE]),
    ("structure_pfk_table", "structural", [PFK_FILE]),
    ("values_single_gene_deletions", "scientific", [GENE_FILE]),
    ("values_single_reaction_deletions", "scientific", [REACTION_FILE]),
    ("values_double_reaction_deletions", "scientific", [DOUBLE_FILE]),
    ("values_pfk_knockout_optima", "scientific", [PFK_FILE]),
    ("cross_table_consistency", "scientific", ALL_FILES),
]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--reference-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--submission-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    results = {}

    def record(check_id, passed, message):
        results[check_id] = (bool(passed), str(message))

    # trusted model population (input-grounded coverage)
    trusted_dir = os.environ.get("BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR", "")
    population_error = None
    genes = reactions = None
    try:
        genes, reactions = _model_population(trusted_dir)
    except Exception as exc:
        population_error = "cannot derive model population from trusted input: %s" % exc

    gene_keys = set(genes) if genes is not None else None
    reaction_keys = set(reactions) if reactions is not None else None
    double_keys = _double_population(reactions) if reactions is not None else None
    if genes is not None:
        for identifier in ("b1723", "b3916"):
            if identifier not in gene_keys:
                population_error = "gene %s missing from trusted model" % identifier
        if "PFK" not in reaction_keys:
            population_error = "reaction PFK missing from trusted model"

    expected = {
        GENE_FILE: (gene_keys, "every gene defined in the supplied model"),
        REACTION_FILE: (reaction_keys, "every reaction defined in the supplied model"),
        DOUBLE_FILE: (double_keys, "all singleton and unordered pairwise reaction sets"),
        PFK_FILE: (set(PFK_LABELS), "exactly the four defined scenario labels"),
    }

    # load reference and submission tables
    ref = {}
    ref_errors = {}
    for name in ALL_FILES:
        table, err = _load(os.path.join(args.reference_dir, name))
        ref[name] = table
        ref_errors[name] = err

    sub = {}
    sub_errors = {}
    for name in ALL_FILES:
        table, err = _load(os.path.join(args.submission_dir, name))
        sub[name] = table
        sub_errors[name] = err

    # -------------------------------------------------------- structural checks
    structure_ids = {
        GENE_FILE: "structure_single_gene_table",
        REACTION_FILE: "structure_single_reaction_table",
        DOUBLE_FILE: "structure_double_reaction_table",
        PFK_FILE: "structure_pfk_table",
    }
    for name in ALL_FILES:
        check_id = structure_ids[name]
        want, description = expected[name]
        if sub_errors[name] is not None:
            record(check_id, False, sub_errors[name])
            continue
        if population_error is not None:
            record(check_id, False, population_error)
            continue
        keys = set(sub[name])
        if keys != want:
            missing = sorted(want - keys)
            extra = sorted(keys - want)
            detail = []
            if missing:
                detail.append("missing %d (e.g. %s)" % (len(missing), missing[:3]))
            if extra:
                detail.append("unexpected %d (e.g. %s)" % (len(extra), extra[:3]))
            record(
                check_id,
                False,
                "knockout key set does not cover %s: %s"
                % (description, "; ".join(detail)),
            )
            continue
        record(
            check_id,
            True,
            "%s: header, %d unique rows and the full knockout population are present"
            % (name, len(sub[name])),
        )

    # -------------------------------------------------------- scientific checks
    value_ids = {
        GENE_FILE: "values_single_gene_deletions",
        REACTION_FILE: "values_single_reaction_deletions",
        DOUBLE_FILE: "values_double_reaction_deletions",
        PFK_FILE: "values_pfk_knockout_optima",
    }
    for name in ALL_FILES:
        check_id = value_ids[name]
        if sub_errors[name] is not None:
            record(check_id, False, sub_errors[name])
            continue
        if ref_errors[name] is not None:
            record(check_id, False, "reference unreadable, comparison not performed: %s" % ref_errors[name])
            continue
        if population_error is not None:
            record(check_id, False, population_error)
            continue
        if set(sub[name]) != expected[name][0]:
            record(check_id, False, "key set invalid; see the structural check")
            continue
        problems = _compare(ref[name], sub[name])
        record(check_id, not problems, _summary(problems))

    # ---------------------------------------------------- cross-file consistency
    gene_t = sub[GENE_FILE] if sub_errors[GENE_FILE] is None else {}
    reaction_t = sub[REACTION_FILE] if sub_errors[REACTION_FILE] is None else {}
    double_t = sub[DOUBLE_FILE] if sub_errors[DOUBLE_FILE] is None else {}
    pfk_t = sub[PFK_FILE] if sub_errors[PFK_FILE] is None else {}
    problems = []
    if population_error is not None:
        problems.append(population_error)
    else:
        for rid in sorted(reaction_keys):
            left, right = double_t.get(rid), reaction_t.get(rid)
            if left is None or right is None:
                problems.append("missing key %s" % rid)
                continue
            if left[1] != right[1]:
                problems.append("%s: status %r vs single-reaction %r" % (rid, left[1], right[1]))
                continue
            if left[0] == "" or right[0] == "":
                if left[0] != right[0]:
                    problems.append("%s: growth presence differs between tables" % rid)
                continue
            lv, lerr = _parse_growth(left[0])
            rv, rerr = _parse_growth(right[0])
            if lerr or rerr or not _close(lv, rv):
                problems.append("%s: double-table singleton disagrees with single-reaction row" % rid)

        pairs = [
            ("", GENE_FILE, "b1723"),
            ("PFK", REACTION_FILE, "PFK"),
            ("b1723", GENE_FILE, "b1723"),
            ("b1723;b3916", REACTION_FILE, "PFK"),
        ]
        for pfk_label, other_file, other_key in pairs:
            other_t = gene_t if other_file == GENE_FILE else reaction_t
            left, right = pfk_t.get(pfk_label), other_t.get(other_key)
            if left is None or right is None:
                problems.append("missing key %r in %s relation" % (pfk_label, other_file))
                continue
            if left[1] != right[1]:
                problems.append("%s: status %r vs %s row %r" % (pfk_label, left[1], other_file, right[1]))
                continue
            if left[0] == "" or right[0] == "":
                if left[0] != right[0]:
                    problems.append("%s: growth presence differs from %s row" % (pfk_label, other_file))
                continue
            lv, lerr = _parse_growth(left[0])
            rv, rerr = _parse_growth(right[0])
            if lerr or rerr or not _close(lv, rv):
                problems.append("%s: growth disagrees with %s row" % (pfk_label, other_file))
    record("cross_table_consistency", not problems, _summary(problems))

    report = {
        "passed": all(passed for passed, _ in results.values()),
        "checks": [
            {"id": check_id, "passed": results[check_id][0], "message": results[check_id][1]}
            for check_id, _, _ in CHECKS
        ],
    }
    with open(args.report, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(report, handle, indent=2)
        handle.write("\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import argparse
import math
import os


def _format_growth(value):
    if value is None:
        return ""
    value = float(value)
    if math.isnan(value):
        return ""
    return repr(value)


def _format_knockouts(ids):
    return ";".join(sorted(str(identifier) for identifier in ids))


def _frame_rows(frame):
    if "ids" in frame.columns:
        ids_series = frame["ids"].tolist()
    else:
        ids_series = frame.index.tolist()
    growth_series = frame["growth"].tolist()
    status_series = frame["status"].tolist()
    rows = []
    for ids, growth, status in zip(ids_series, growth_series, status_series):
        rows.append(
            (_format_knockouts(ids), _format_growth(growth), str(status))
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: row[0])
    return rows


def _write_csv(path, header, rows):
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write(header + "\n")
        for row in rows:
            handle.write(",".join(row) + "\n")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    from cobra.io import read_sbml_model
    from cobra.flux_analysis import (
        single_gene_deletion,
        single_reaction_deletion,
        double_reaction_deletion,
    )

    model = read_sbml_model(os.path.join(args.input_dir, "e_coli_core.xml"))
    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    gene_frame = single_gene_deletion(model)
    reaction_frame = single_reaction_deletion(model)
    double_frame = double_reaction_deletion(model)

    header = "knockouts,growth,status"
    _write_csv(
        os.path.join(args.output_dir, "single_gene_deletions.csv"),
        header,
        _frame_rows(gene_frame),
    )
    _write_csv(
        os.path.join(args.output_dir, "single_reaction_deletions.csv"),
        header,
        _frame_rows(reaction_frame),
    )
    _write_csv(
        os.path.join(args.output_dir, "double_reaction_deletions.csv"),
        header,
        _frame_rows(double_frame),
    )

    # Phosphofructokinase redundancy scenarios, mirroring the defined semantics:
    # wild type, PFK reaction knockout, pfkA gene knockout, and the
    # simultaneous pfkA + pfkB double gene knockout (sequential knockouts of
    # both genes on the same model within one context).
    rows = []
    solution = model.optimize()
    rows.append(("", _format_growth(solution.objective_value), solution.status))
    with model:
        model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()
        solution = model.optimize()
        rows.append(("PFK", _format_growth(solution.objective_value), solution.status))
    with model:
        model.genes.b1723.knock_out()
        solution = model.optimize()
        rows.append(("b1723", _format_growth(solution.objective_value), solution.status))
        model.genes.b3916.knock_out()
        solution = model.optimize()
        rows.append(
            ("b1723;b3916", _format_growth(solution.objective_value), solution.status)
        )
    _write_csv(os.path.join(args.output_dir, "pfk_knockout_optima.csv"), header, rows)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Task Description:

Growth effects of gene and reaction knockouts in the E. coli core metabolic model

Objective

You are given the curated "textbook" E. coli core metabolic model (BiGG id e_coli_core) as an SBML file. Using flux balance analysis (FBA), determine how every possible single-gene deletion, every single-reaction deletion, every pairwise reaction deletion, and four specific knockout scenarios that illustrate gene-level redundancy for phosphofructokinase affect the maximal achievable growth.

By "growth" we mean the optimal value of the model's biomass objective (the raw LP objective value; no rounding, clamping or sign correction). For every knockout scenario, report that optimum together with the status reported by the LP solve (e.g. optimal or infeasible).

Supplied input

  • inputs/e_coli_core.xml — the E. coli core metabolic model in SBML format, including its biomass objective reaction and gene–protein–reaction (GPR) associations. Use the model exactly as supplied; do not modify it, its medium, bounds or objective.

Knockout semantics

  • Reaction knockout: the reaction carries no flux; its flux is constrained to zero in both directions.
  • Gene knockout: a reaction is disabled only if its GPR rule evaluates to false once the knocked-out gene(s) are removed. If a reaction has a remaining functional isozyme gene (an OR in the GPR), the reaction still carries flux; a gene whose removal disables no reaction therefore has no growth effect even though the gene is knocked out.

Required outputs

Produce four CSV files, all with the columns knockouts,growth,status:

  • knockouts: the identifier(s) of the knocked-out entity, exactly as defined in the supplied model. For a knockout of multiple entities, the ids are sorted lexicographically and joined with ; (e.g. b1723;b3916, Biomass_Ecoli_core;LDH_D); a single-entity knockout uses just that entity's id.
  • growth: the optimal objective value of the LP after the knockout, as reported by the solver at full double precision, with no rounding, clamping or sign correction. Tiny negative values of magnitude around 1e-14 that arise from solver noise are expected and must be reported as-is. Leave this field empty when the knockout makes the problem infeasible.
  • status: the LP solve status string, e.g. optimal or infeasible.

1. single_gene_deletions.csv

One row for every gene defined in the supplied model (137 genes), including genes whose deletion disables no reaction.

2. single_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for every reaction defined in the supplied model (95 reactions, including boundary/exchange reactions).

3. double_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for each distinct knockout set {r_i, r_j} obtained by pairing every reaction in the model with every reaction in the model and reducing each ordered pair to an unordered set; the i = j cases contribute the single-reaction sets {r_i}. This yields the 95 singleton sets plus all C(95,2) = 4465 pairs, i.e. 4560 rows. Do not apply gene-level GPR logic here — both reactions are knocked out directly.

4. pfk_knockout_optima.csv

Exactly four rows, with the same column convention and an empty knockouts field for the no-knockout row:

  • (empty) — the unmodified (wild-type) model, no knockout;
  • PFK — the PFK reaction knocked out;
  • b1723 — gene b1723 (pfkA) knocked out;
  • b1723;b3916 — genes b1723 (pfkA) and b3916 (pfkB) knocked out simultaneously.

These quantify isozyme redundancy: the isozyme pfkB can compensate for a pfkA deletion, but not when both genes are removed.

Conventions

  • Row order in every file carries no scientific meaning; any row ordering is acceptable.
  • Growth is reported in the model's native biomass-objective units (the raw LP objective value).
  • Use the knockout populations exactly as defined above; do not skip entities that have no reaction associations or no growth effect.
  • Do not round any value (growth is written at full double precision).

Environment and resources

CPU only (up to 4 cores), 8 GiB RAM, no network access. Your program must complete within 600 seconds. Any software stack that satisfies the definitions above is acceptable; the results, not the tool, are what is compared.

Exact acceptance criteria (including numerical tolerances appropriate for LP-solver variation) are finalized separately during validation before the contract takes effect; produce results faithful to the definitions above.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules for the knockout-FBA outputs

Files compared. Exactly the four declared output files, each read as a comma-delimited UTF-8 CSV at its declared path relative to the supplied output root (no fallback directories, no extra outputs/ layer): single_gene_deletions.csv, single_reaction_deletions.csv, double_reaction_deletions.csv, pfk_knockout_optima.csv.

CSV syntax. Each file must carry exactly the header knockouts,growth,status and every data row must have exactly three fields (quoted empty fields and decimal values following standard CSV quoting are ordinary data; blank records are not permitted). Values must be plain decimal numbers in a standard fixed or scientific notation; hexadecimal, inf, nan or other nonfinite/invalid numerics fail. The growth field must be empty exactly when the solve is not optimal; for optimal rows it must contain a finite number.

Row alignment and ordering. Comparison is by the knockouts key, not by file position: any row order is acceptable. Each knockout label must appear exactly once; duplicate labels fail. Labels for multi-entity knockouts are the lexicographically sorted ids joined with ;; single-entity knockouts use the bare id. The empty wild-type row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv uses an empty knockouts field.

Coverage (input-grounded). The knockout population is derived from the supplied model e_coli_core.xml, not from the reference file: single_gene_deletions.csv must contain exactly one row per gene defined in the model; single_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per reaction defined in the model (including boundary/exchange reactions); double_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per single-reaction set and per unordered reaction pair (the 95 singletons plus all C(95,2) pairs, i.e. 4560 rows); pfk_knockout_optima.csv exactly the four rows "", PFK, b1723, b1723;b3916. Missing rows, extra rows or a different population fail.

Status comparison. The status string is compared exactly (e.g. optimal, infeasible); any status text that differs from the reference status for that knockout fails.

Numeric comparison. For each row with reference growth r and submission growth s, acceptance requires |s - r| <= max(1e-9 * max(|r|, |s|), 1e-11). The reference value is part of the denominator convention (the larger of the two magnitudes). This bound covers ordinary double-precision serialization and cross-solver variation, including the tiny (below ~5e-13 in magnitude) near-zero optima whose sign or exact zero-vs-noise value is solver-dependent; it does not license rounding to fewer significant digits, since genuine optimum differences between distinct knockout sets in this model are separated from that noise by several orders of magnitude. A growth value must not be clamped, sign-corrected or rounded to a coarser precision than that bound permits. An infeasible solve must be reported with an empty growth field, not zero.

Cross-file consistency. The following relations between the submitted files are enforced with the same tolerance: each single-reaction set row of double_reaction_deletions.csv must agree with the corresponding row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the PFK row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the PFK row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the b1723 gene row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv; the wild-type row must agree in growth with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv (isozyme pfkB compensates pfkA removal); and the b1723;b3916 row must agree with the PFK reaction-knockout rows (removing both PFK genes disables exactly the PFK reaction, which the supplied model's GPR associations define via b1723 and b3916 on PFK only).

No software stack is prescribed; any implementation producing these values is acceptable, and agreement of the alternative stacks used during validation is demonstrated, not assumed for others.

Task directories

import cobra, time, itertools
m=cobra.io.read_sbml_model('/workspace/inputs/e_coli_core.xml')
print('reaction IDs sample:', [r.id for r in m.reactions[:10]])
print('gene IDs sample:', [g.id for g in m.genes[:10]])
print('PFK reaction:', m.reactions.PFK.id, m.reactions.PFK.gene_reaction_rule)

def solve(label, kind, ids):
    with m:
        if kind == 'reaction':
            for x in ids: m.reactions.get_by_id(x).bounds = (0, 0)
        else:
            for x in ids: m.genes.get_by_id(x).knock_out()
        s = m.optimize()
        print(label, kind, repr(s.status), repr(s.objective_value),
              'disabled:', [r.id for r in m.reactions if not r.functional])

solve('WT', 'gene', [])
solve('PFK', 'reaction', ['PFK'])
solve('b1723', 'gene', ['b1723'])
solve('b1723;b3916', 'gene', ['b1723', 'b3916'])

rs=[r.id for r in m.reactions]
pairs=list(itertools.combinations(rs[:20],2))[:100]
t=time.perf_counter(); n_infeasible=0
for a,b in pairs:
    with m:
        m.reactions.get_by_id(a).bounds=(0,0)
        m.reactions.get_by_id(b).bounds=(0,0)
        s=m.optimize()
        if s.status != 'optimal': n_infeasible += 1
print('benchmark_seconds', time.perf_counter()-t)
print('solves', len(pairs), 'non-optimal', n_infeasible)

#!/opt/venv/bin/python
import csv
import itertools
import math
import os
import time

import cobra

INPUT = '/workspace/inputs/e_coli_core.xml'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/workspace/outputs'


def solve_current(model):
    solution = model.optimize()
    if solution.status == 'optimal':
        value = solution.objective_value
        if value is None or not math.isfinite(value):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f'Optimal solve has invalid objective value: {value!r}'
            )
        # repr(float) is Python's round-trip-preserving shortest representation.
        growth = repr(float(value))
    else:
        growth = ''
    return solution.status, growth


def gene_knockout(model, gene_ids):
    with model:
        for gene_id in gene_ids:
            model.genes.get_by_id(gene_id).knock_out()
        return solve_current(model)


def reaction_knockout(model, reaction_ids):
    with model:
        for reaction_id in reaction_ids:
            model.reactions.get_by_id(reaction_id).bounds = (0, 0)
        return solve_current(model)


def write_csv(path, rows):
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle, lineterminator='\n')
        writer.writerow(['knockouts', 'growth', 'status'])
        writer.writerows(rows)


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    model = cobra.io.read_sbml_model(INPUT)
    model.solver = 'glpk'
    print(
        f'Loaded {model.id}: {len(model.reactions)} reactions, '
        f'{len(model.genes)} genes',
        flush=True,
    )

    started = time.perf_counter()

    # Every model gene, including genes whose deletion disables no reaction.
    gene_rows = []
    for gene in model.genes:
        gene_rows.append((gene.id, *gene_knockout(model, [gene.id])))
    write_csv(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'single_gene_deletions.csv'), gene_rows)
    print(f'Wrote {len(gene_rows)} gene deletions', flush=True)

    # Every model reaction, including exchanges/boundary reactions.
    reaction_ids = [reaction.id for reaction in model.reactions]
    reaction_rows = []
    for reaction_id in reaction_ids:
        reaction_rows.append((reaction_id, *reaction_knockout(model, [reaction_id])))
    write_csv(
        os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'single_reaction_deletions.csv'), reaction_rows
    )
    print(f'Wrote {len(reaction_rows)} single reaction deletions', flush=True)

    # All 95 singleton sets and every distinct unordered reaction pair.
    double_rows = []
    for left, right in itertools.combinations_with_replacement(
        sorted(reaction_ids), 2
    ):
        ids = sorted({left, right})
        label = ';'.join(ids)
        double_rows.append((label, *reaction_knockout(model, ids)))
    write_csv(
        os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'double_reaction_deletions.csv'), double_rows
    )
    print(f'Wrote {len(double_rows)} double reaction deletion sets', flush=True)

    # Wild type, direct PFK reaction deletion, and PFK isozyme gene cases.
    pfk_rows = [
        ('', *solve_current(model)),
        ('PFK', *reaction_knockout(model, ['PFK'])),
        ('b1723', *gene_knockout(model, ['b1723'])),
        ('b1723;b3916', *gene_knockout(model, ['b1723', 'b3916'])),
    ]
    write_csv(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, 'pfk_knockout_optima.csv'), pfk_rows)
    print(f'Wrote {len(pfk_rows)} PFK scenarios', flush=True)
    print(f'Elapsed: {time.perf_counter() - started:.3f} s', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import csv
import itertools
import math
import os

import cobra

base = '/workspace/outputs'
model = cobra.io.read_sbml_model('/workspace/inputs/e_coli_core.xml')
gene_ids = {g.id for g in model.genes}
reaction_ids = {r.id for r in model.reactions}
expected_counts = {
    'single_gene_deletions.csv': 137,
    'single_reaction_deletions.csv': 95,
    'double_reaction_deletions.csv': 4560,
    'pfk_knockout_optima.csv': 4,
}

def load(name):
    path = os.path.join(base, name)
    with open(path, newline='', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
        reader = csv.reader(handle)
        assert next(reader) == ['knockouts', 'growth', 'status'], (name, 'header')
        raw = list(reader)
    assert len(raw) == expected_counts[name], (name, len(raw), expected_counts[name])
    assert all(len(row) == 3 and any(field for field in row) for row in raw), name
    result = {row[0]: {'growth': row[1], 'status': row[2]} for row in raw}
    assert len(result) == len(raw), (name, 'duplicate labels')
    for label, row in result.items():
        assert row['status'] in {'optimal', 'infeasible'}, (name, label, row)
        if row['status'] == 'optimal':
            assert row['growth'] and math.isfinite(float(row['growth'])), (name, label, row)
        else:
            assert row['growth'] == '', (name, label, row)
    return result

genes = load('single_gene_deletions.csv')
singles = load('single_reaction_deletions.csv')
doubles = load('double_reaction_deletions.csv')
pfk = load('pfk_knockout_optima.csv')

assert set(genes) == gene_ids
assert set(singles) == reaction_ids
expected_double_labels = {
    ';'.join(pair)
    for pair in itertools.combinations_with_replacement(sorted(reaction_ids), 2)
}
assert set(doubles) == expected_double_labels

for label, single in singles.items():
    double = doubles[label]
    assert double['status'] == single['status'], label
    if single['status'] == 'optimal':
        a = float(single['growth'])
        b = float(double['growth'])
        tolerance = max(1e-9 * max(abs(a), abs(b)), 1e-11)
        assert abs(a - b) <= tolerance, (label, a, b)

assert set(pfk) == {'', 'PFK', 'b1723', 'b1723;b3916'}
assert pfk['']['status'] == genes['b1723']['status'] == 'optimal'
assert abs(float(pfk['']['growth']) - float(genes['b1723']['growth'])) <= 1e-10
assert pfk['PFK']['status'] == singles['PFK']['status'] == pfk['b1723;b3916']['status'] == 'optimal'
assert abs(float(pfk['PFK']['growth']) - float(singles['PFK']['growth'])) <= 1e-10
assert abs(float(pfk['b1723;b3916']['growth']) - float(singles['PFK']['growth'])) <= 1e-10

assert sorted(os.listdir(base)) == sorted(expected_counts)
print('FINAL VALIDATION PASSED')
for name, data in [
    ('single_gene_deletions.csv', genes),
    ('single_reaction_deletions.csv', singles),
    ('double_reaction_deletions.csv', doubles),
]:
    statuses = {status: sum(row['status'] == status for row in data.values())
                for status in sorted({row['status'] for row in data.values()})}
    print(f'{name}: {len(data)} rows, statuses={statuses}')
print('PFK scenarios:')
for label in ['', 'PFK', 'b1723', 'b1723;b3916']:
    print(label or '<wild type>', pfk[label])

   "source": [
    "A commonly asked question when analyzing metabolic models is what will happen if a certain reaction was not allowed to have any flux at all. This can tested using cobrapy by"

   ],
   "source": [
    "print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())\n",
    "with cobra_model:\n",
    "    cobra_model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()\n",

   ]

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",

# ---
# jupyter:

# # Simulating Deletions

import pandas
from time import time

from cobra.io import load_model
from cobra.flux_analysis import (
    single_gene_deletion, single_reaction_deletion, double_gene_deletion,
    double_reaction_deletion)

cobra_model = load_model("textbook")
ecoli_model = load_model("iJO1366")

# ## Knocking out single genes and reactions

# A commonly asked question when analyzing metabolic models is what will happen if a certain reaction was not allowed to have any flux at all. This can tested using cobrapy by

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()
    print('pfk knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# For evaluating genetic manipulation strategies, it is more interesting to examine what happens if given genes are knocked out as doing so can affect no reactions in case of redundancy, or more reactions if gene when is participating in more than one reaction.

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.genes.b1723.knock_out()
    print('pfkA knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())
    cobra_model.genes.b3916.knock_out()
    print('pfkB knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# ## Single Deletions

# Perform all single gene deletions on a model

deletion_results = single_gene_deletion(cobra_model)

# These can also be done for only a subset of genes

single_gene_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[:20])

# This can also be done for reactions

single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[:20])

# ## Double Deletions

# Double deletions run in a similar way.

double_gene_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[-5:]).round(4)

# By default, the double deletion function will automatically use multiprocessing, splitting the task over up to 4 cores if they are available. The number of cores can be manually specified as well. Setting use of a single core will disable use of the multiprocessing library, which often aids debugging.

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=2)
t1 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 2 cores" % t1)

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=1)
t2 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 1 core" % t2)

print("Speedup of %.2fx" % (t2 / t1))

# Double deletions can also be run for reactions.

double_reaction_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[2:7]).round(4)

# ## Accessing individual deletion results
#
# Note that the indices for deletions are python [set](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/stdtypes.html#set-types-set-frozenset) objects. This is the appropriate type since the order of deletions does not matter. Deleting reaction 1 and reaction 2 will have the same effect as deleting reaction 2 and reaction 1. 
#
# To make it easier to access results all DataFrames returned by COBRAPpy deletion functions have a `knockout` indexer that makes that a bit simpler. Each entry in the indexer is treated as a single deletion entry. So you need to pass sets for double deletions.

single = single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)
double = double_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)

print(single.knockout["ATPM"])
print(double.knockout[{"ATPM", "TKT1"}])

# This can be used to get several deletions at once and will also work for Reaction or Gene objects (depending on what you deleted) directly.

atpm = cobra_model.reactions.ATPM
tkt1 = cobra_model.reactions.TKT1
pfk = cobra_model.reactions.PFK

print(single.knockout[atpm, tkt1, pfk])
print(double.knockout[{atpm, tkt1}, {atpm, pfk}, {atpm}])

Return only the export code, not an edited or recopied source script. The controller appends it to the untouched baseline. This stage does not manage or execute the environment. There is one creation call and at most one repair after programmatic validation rejects the response or a controlled execution finds an export-code exception. These share one repair, not one each. If the controller returns validation feedback, return a complete corrected ReferencePlan, including unchanged fields. Keep the original scientific source and the export-only boundary fixed. A valid first response needs no repair. Keep explanations brief and nonduplicated.

Inputs

The user message supplies:

  • baseline_script: the complete, unmodified Python script from deterministic notebook conversion, with the original Markdown narrative retained as comments.
  • source: notebook identity and provenance.
  • conversion: the conversion receipt and source/script identities.
  • limits: the intended execution environment and resource/time limits.
  • During a runtime repair only, runtime_validation: the previous complete plan and the recorded execution error. Use this feedback to correct serialization of the same selected results. Preserve artifacts and excluded_outputs exactly, including paths and source evidence. Do not fix the analysis or select different results. Observations in an error log can be partial; do not invent data layout or new scientific computation to fill gaps.

You do not receive saved notebook outputs, embedded images, scientific data contents or tool access. A path or URL is not evidence that a resource has been inspected. Select terminal scientific results

First identify the scientific conclusions or end products the source aims to produce. Use its narrative and how results are interpreted, not a list of its sections, functions or stored variables. Include the independent scientific outcomes of all analysis branches in one task. Preparatory and diagnostic steps supporting those outcomes are not additional branches that need an export.

For each candidate result, distinguish its role:

  • An endpoint reports a scientific finding or final representation that the source interprets in its own right.
  • An intermediate prepares data or supplies another analysis step.
  • A diagnostic checks data quality, model fit or parameter choices in support of the analysis. Its being displayed, discussed or retained does not by itself make it a scientific endpoint.

Select the endpoints. A value used downstream can still qualify when the source also interprets it as an independent result; a value with no downstream consumer can still be only a diagnostic. Do not equate endpoints with either literal execution-graph leaves or objects surviving to the end. If the source does not establish an independent endpoint role, explain the exclusion or uncertainty rather than adding an export just for completeness.

Then locate the selected results in existing named variables or fields in the ORIGINAL script. They must still hold the intended values at script completion. If a result has been overwritten, deleted or is out of scope, explain its unavailability for append-only export; do not insert earlier captures or rerun computation to recover it. Variable scope or persistence is not scientific eligibility. Record an independently interpreted endpoint as still required, with its original source location and the state needed to recover it. A later construction worker may faithfully recompute it only when task policy permits; do not claim that recovery has happened or promise it is feasible. A result displayed in a plot can qualify if its values already exist outside the plotting function. Values computed only inside plotting functions cannot.

Select fields by their scientific role before choosing a file format. This rule applies recursively: a table inside a mixed analysis object can itself mix final results with inputs, preprocessing statistics and diagnostics. Export only the selected endpoint fields and the identifiers/context needed to interpret them; do not copy all columns or dump a whole object because it is convenient. A standalone result table or embedding may be exported whole when its contents meet this rule. Preserve its meaningful result fields and identifiers, explaining any omissions. Selecting stored fields is allowed; changing the analyzed population or adding scientific computation is not. Output size alone does not determine eligibility.

In excluded_outputs, distinguish source-backed scientific non-targets from required endpoints unavailable to this export step. For each unavailable result, identify its original computation and why the intended value is not accessible at completion. This is a recovery handoff, not permission to omit that endpoint from the eventual task. Do not enumerate every processing step. If no eligible terminal result can be exported, return disposition=reject. Excluding an output never permits skipping its original computation.

Save existing values only

Serialization means writing existing values and their identifiers to files. Use native writers or straightforward file-format conversion. Preserve values, identifiers, labels and ordering of the selected final-state results. A later filtered or overwritten object does not preserve an earlier result merely because it has the same variable name.

Prefer the selected stored result's own writer, including a writer on an already stored child table or array after selecting endpoint fields. Do not rebuild or wrap that result in another framework-specific container just to save it when the selected value already has an appropriate writer. A new wrapper or separate package-level export API can impose an unnecessary version requirement that conflicts with the original analysis. If a conversion helper is necessary, explain that necessity and leave unsupported runtime/API assumptions explicit; do not claim compatibility without execution evidence.

Do not add scientific computation for exports: no new filtering, ranking, aggregation, normalization, scaling, statistical tests or reconstruction of values computed inside plotting functions. Do not capture a previously unnamed standalone expression by assigning it to a new variable. Values inside an already named source object are eligible; a result held only inside a plotting function is not. Do not change plotting calls or add figure capture. Explain excluded plot-only results instead of claiming their numerical content was exported.

File-writing code may introduce output paths and serialization helpers, but not new scientific results. Put any needed imports in the appended export code, using names that do not overwrite source results. Do not recompute an analysis or call it again to obtain an export. Do not change the original inputs, methods, parameters, randomness, filtering, annotations, error handling or execution order. Keep the original analysis and comments intact, including branches whose outputs are excluded. Preserve source-level reductions; add none. Do not suppress analysis errors.

Required response

  • disposition: prepare or reject.
  • explanation: a brief reason and account of the added export code.
  • export_code: only the Python code to append at the end of the baseline, including any imports needed for saving files. Do not include the baseline, patches, insertion instructions, Markdown fences or future imports. Write endpoint files under /work/outputs, creating that directory if needed. Use only eligible original results still accessible at completion. For disposition=reject, this field may be empty.
  • artifacts: one inventory of endpoint files. Each entry has a path relative to /work/outputs (for example result.csv for /work/outputs/result.csv), a brief description of the terminal result, and source_evidence explaining why this is an endpoint based on the source analysis goals, and identifying the existing variable or object field and where the original script produces it. Cite the source narrative or use that establishes its endpoint role; mere persistence or a function name is not evidence of that role. Prefer interoperable formats. Several existing endpoint values may share a file if their identities remain explicit. Keep this inventory consistent with the export code: every declared path must be written under that exact name, with no placeholder or undeclared output filenames. Check that correspondence before returning the response.
  • excluded_outputs: meaningful scientific non-targets with their source-backed reasons, and independently interpreted endpoints unavailable for append-only export with the source location and recovery gap. State which kind each entry is in its existing explanation; do not add another inventory or new fields. Unavailability does not settle eventual task coverage. Do not enumerate every intermediate.
  • unresolved_assumptions: specific questions for subsequent inspection or execution; do not invent observed dimensions, values, timing or resource use.

The controller preserves the returned export code and constructs the reference script as the original baseline, two newlines, then the export code. It checks response structure and combined Python syntax without executing code, and computes the source diff, file sizes and hashes. Do not generate those records. These checks do not prove terminal-result selection, scientific fidelity or successful execution.

Boundary with execution

The execution stage owns dependency discovery and installation, the Python project and uv lockfile, system packages, input downloads, caches and offline path adaptation. It can use an LLM with tools to inspect and diagnose concrete failures. Ordinary script execution is programmatic. Preparation must not return an environment manifest or staging script, install packages, rewrite retrieval code, choose package versions or claim an environment works. Leave original input-loading code unchanged for execution-stage adaptation and review.

The later scientific run remains CPU-only and offline, with original inputs staged during network-enabled setup. The supplied limits apply; uncertainty about fit is an execution question, not permission to simplify the analysis. Original responses and validation failures are preserved. The controller may request one corrected response for a validation failure; this does not authorize repairing the scientific source or retrying transport failures. Source analysis defects must not be repaired by changing the science. Distinguish a known defect from an untested assumption and explain rejection precisely.

import os as _export_os
import pandas as _export_pd

_export_dir = "/work/outputs"
_export_os.makedirs(_export_dir, exist_ok=True)


def _write_deletion_results(frame, filename):
    export_frame = frame.copy()
    export_frame.index = _export_pd.Index(
        [";".join(sorted(str(identifier) for identifier in knockout_ids))
         for knockout_ids in export_frame.index],
        name="knockouts",
    )
    export_frame.to_csv(_export_os.path.join(_export_dir, filename))


_write_deletion_results(deletion_results, "single_gene_deletions.csv")
_write_deletion_results(single, "single_reaction_deletions.csv")
_write_deletion_results(double, "double_reaction_deletions.csv")

# ---
# jupyter:
#   jupytext:
#     text_representation:
#       extension: .py
#       format_name: nomarker
#       format_version: '1.0'

#   kernelspec:
#     display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)

# # Simulating Deletions

import pandas
from time import time

from cobra.io import load_model
from cobra.flux_analysis import (
    single_gene_deletion, single_reaction_deletion, double_gene_deletion,
    double_reaction_deletion)

cobra_model = load_model("textbook")
ecoli_model = load_model("iJO1366")

# ## Knocking out single genes and reactions

# A commonly asked question when analyzing metabolic models is what will happen if a certain reaction was not allowed to have any flux at all. This can tested using cobrapy by

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()
    print('pfk knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# For evaluating genetic manipulation strategies, it is more interesting to examine what happens if given genes are knocked out as doing so can affect no reactions in case of redundancy, or more reactions if gene when is participating in more than one reaction.

print('complete model: ', cobra_model.optimize())
with cobra_model:
    cobra_model.genes.b1723.knock_out()
    print('pfkA knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())
    cobra_model.genes.b3916.knock_out()
    print('pfkB knocked out: ', cobra_model.optimize())

# ## Single Deletions

# Perform all single gene deletions on a model

deletion_results = single_gene_deletion(cobra_model)

# These can also be done for only a subset of genes

single_gene_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[:20])

# This can also be done for reactions

single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[:20])

# ## Double Deletions

# Double deletions run in a similar way.

double_gene_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.genes[-5:]).round(4)

# By default, the double deletion function will automatically use multiprocessing, splitting the task over up to 4 cores if they are available. The number of cores can be manually specified as well. Setting use of a single core will disable use of the multiprocessing library, which often aids debugging.

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=2)
t1 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 2 cores" % t1)

start = time()  # start timer()
double_gene_deletion(
    ecoli_model, ecoli_model.genes[:25], processes=1)
t2 = time() - start
print("Double gene deletions for 200 genes completed in "
      "%.2f sec with 1 core" % t2)

print("Speedup of %.2fx" % (t2 / t1))

# Double deletions can also be run for reactions.

double_reaction_deletion(
    cobra_model, cobra_model.reactions[2:7]).round(4)

# ## Accessing individual deletion results
#
# Note that the indices for deletions are python [set](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/stdtypes.html#set-types-set-frozenset) objects. This is the appropriate type since the order of deletions does not matter. Deleting reaction 1 and reaction 2 will have the same effect as deleting reaction 2 and reaction 1. 
#
# To make it easier to access results all DataFrames returned by COBRAPpy deletion functions have a `knockout` indexer that makes that a bit simpler. Each entry in the indexer is treated as a single deletion entry. So you need to pass sets for double deletions.

single = single_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)
double = double_reaction_deletion(cobra_model)

print(single.knockout["ATPM"])
print(double.knockout[{"ATPM", "TKT1"}])

# This can be used to get several deletions at once and will also work for Reaction or Gene objects (depending on what you deleted) directly.

atpm = cobra_model.reactions.ATPM
tkt1 = cobra_model.reactions.TKT1
pfk = cobra_model.reactions.PFK

print(single.knockout[atpm, tkt1, pfk])
print(double.knockout[{atpm, tkt1}, {atpm, pfk}, {atpm}])





import os as _export_os
import pandas as _export_pd

_export_dir = "/work/outputs"
_export_os.makedirs(_export_dir, exist_ok=True)


def _write_deletion_results(frame, filename):
    export_frame = frame.copy()
    export_frame.index = _export_pd.Index(
        [";".join(sorted(str(identifier) for identifier in knockout_ids))
         for knockout_ids in export_frame.index],
        name="knockouts",
    )
    export_frame.to_csv(_export_os.path.join(_export_dir, filename))


_write_deletion_results(deletion_results, "single_gene_deletions.csv")
_write_deletion_results(single, "single_reaction_deletions.csv")
_write_deletion_results(double, "double_reaction_deletions.csv")
