{
  "disposition": "ready",
  "code": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Growth effects of gene/reaction knockouts in the E. coli core model (FBA).\n\nInputs (read-only):\n    <input-dir>/e_coli_core.xml\n\nOutputs (in <output-dir>):\n    single_gene_deletions.csv\n    single_reaction_deletions.csv\n    double_reaction_deletions.csv\n    pfk_knockout_optima.csv\n\nAll files have columns: knockouts,growth,status\n - knockouts: entity ids, lexicographically sorted, ';'-joined\n - growth: raw LP objective value at full double precision (repr),\n   empty when the solve is not optimal\n - status: solver status string, e.g. 'optimal' or 'infeasible'\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nimport cobra\nfrom cobra.flux_analysis import (\n    double_reaction_deletion,\n    single_gene_deletion,\n    single_reaction_deletion,\n)\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef growth_str(growth, status):\n    \"\"\"Format the raw LP optimum, leaving it empty for non-optimal solves.\"\"\"\n    if status != \"optimal\" or pd.isna(growth):\n        return \"\"\n    return repr(float(growth))\n\n\ndef write_frame(df, path):\n    \"\"\"Convert a cobra deletion DataFrame ('ids','growth','status') to CSV.\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for _, r in df.iterrows():\n        ids = sorted(r[\"ids\"])  # frozenset of ids -> sorted list\n        rows.append({\n            \"knockouts\": \";\".join(ids),\n            \"growth\": growth_str(r[\"growth\"], r[\"status\"]),\n            \"status\": r[\"status\"],\n        })\n    out = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=[\"knockouts\", \"growth\", \"status\"])\n    out.to_csv(path, index=False)\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n\n    model = cobra.io.read_sbml_model(\n        os.path.join(args.input_dir, \"e_coli_core.xml\")\n    )\n\n    # 1. every single gene deletion (137 genes, incl. no-effect genes)\n    res = single_gene_deletion(model, processes=4)\n    write_frame(res, os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"single_gene_deletions.csv\"))\n\n    # 2. every single reaction deletion (95 reactions, incl. exchanges)\n    res = single_reaction_deletion(model, processes=4)\n    write_frame(res, os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"single_reaction_deletions.csv\"))\n\n    # 3. every distinct pair (plus singletons): 95 + C(95,2) = 4560 rows\n    res = double_reaction_deletion(model, processes=4)\n    write_frame(res, os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"double_reaction_deletions.csv\"))\n\n    # 4. PFK / pfkA / pfkB knockout scenarios\n    with model:\n        rows = []\n\n        # wild type (no knockout)\n        growth = model.slim_optimize()\n        rows.append((\"\", growth, model.solver.status))\n\n        # PFK reaction knockout\n        model.reactions.PFK.knock_out()\n        growth = model.slim_optimize()\n        rows.append((\"PFK\", growth, model.solver.status))\n\n        # restore, then gene b1723 (pfkA) knockout only\n    with model:\n        model.genes.b1723.knock_out()\n        growth = model.slim_optimize()\n        rows.append((\"b1723\", growth, model.solver.status))\n\n    with model:\n        # genes b1723 (pfkA) and b3916 (pfkB) knocked out simultaneously\n        model.genes.b1723.knock_out()\n        model.genes.b3916.knock_out()\n        growth = model.slim_optimize()\n        rows.append((\"b1723;b3916\", growth, model.solver.status))\n\n    rows_out = [\n        {\n            \"knockouts\": ko,\n            \"growth\": growth_str(g, st),\n            \"status\": st,\n        }\n        for (ko, g, st) in rows\n    ]\n    pd.DataFrame(rows_out, columns=[\"knockouts\", \"growth\", \"status\"]).to_csv(\n        os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"pfk_knockout_optima.csv\"), index=False\n    )\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
  "rationale": "Uses cobra 0.32.1 (installed) with its native deletion machinery, which implements exactly the public knockout semantics: reaction KO via Reaction.knock_out() (flux forced to zero both directions) and gene KO via Gene.knock_out() (GPR evaluation, isozyme ORs preserved). Model file is loaded unmodified from --input-dir/e_coli_core.xml. single_gene_deletion and single_reaction_deletion cover all model-defined genes/reactants; double_reaction_deletion enumerates all 95+C(95,2)=4560 unordered sets exactly as specified (cobra reduces ordered pairs to frozensets). The four PFK rows are computed by direct model-controlled knockouts (wild type, PFK reaction, gene b1723, genes b1723+B3916) using slim_optimize, reporting the raw LP objective and model.solver.status with model state restored between contexts. growth is written at full double precision via repr (e.g. tiny negatives like -3.64e-15 kept as-is) and is left empty with status 'infeasible' when the LP is infeasible. Boundary choice: cobra's DataFrame (ids/growth/status) is the saved/artifact boundary; ids are sorted lexicographically and ';'-joined, except the m**a prior version's stray line was removed and PFK rows are computed on fresh model contexts. Verified end-to-end on supplied input: 137/95/4560/4 rows, statuses optimal/infeasible consistent with FBA expectations. No confirmation of agreement with the hidden reference has been established - only that outputs match the stated public contract. Runtime ~35 s including a full double-deletion run, well under the 600 s limit."
}

{
  "disposition": "ready",
  "instruction": "## Acceptance rules for the knockout-FBA outputs\n\n**Files compared.** Exactly the four declared output files, each read as a comma-delimited UTF-8 CSV at its declared path relative to the supplied output root (no fallback directories, no extra `outputs/` layer): `single_gene_deletions.csv`, `single_reaction_deletions.csv`, `double_reaction_deletions.csv`, `pfk_knockout_optima.csv`.\n\n**CSV syntax.** Each file must carry exactly the header `knockouts,growth,status` and every data row must have exactly three fields (quoted empty fields and decimal values following standard CSV quoting are ordinary data; blank records are not permitted). Values must be plain decimal numbers in a standard fixed or scientific notation; hexadecimal, `inf`, `nan` or other nonfinite/invalid numerics fail. The `growth` field must be empty exactly when the solve is not `optimal`; for `optimal` rows it must contain a finite number.\n\n**Row alignment and ordering.** Comparison is by the `knockouts` key, not by file position: any row order is acceptable. Each knockout label must appear exactly once; duplicate labels fail. Labels for multi-entity knockouts are the lexicographically sorted ids joined with `;`; single-entity knockouts use the bare id. The empty wild-type row of `pfk_knockout_optima.csv` uses an empty `knockouts` field.\n\n**Coverage (input-grounded).** The knockout population is derived from the supplied model `e_coli_core.xml`, not from the reference file: `single_gene_deletions.csv` must contain exactly one row per gene defined in the model; `single_reaction_deletions.csv` exactly one row per reaction defined in the model (including boundary/exchange reactions); `double_reaction_deletions.csv` exactly one row per single-reaction set and per unordered reaction pair (the 95 singletons plus all C(95,2) pairs, i.e. 4560 rows); `pfk_knockout_optima.csv` exactly the four rows `\"\"`, `PFK`, `b1723`, `b1723;b3916`. Missing rows, extra rows or a different population fail.\n\n**Status comparison.** The `status` string is compared exactly (e.g. `optimal`, `infeasible`); any status text that differs from the reference status for that knockout fails.\n\n**Numeric comparison.** For each row with reference growth `r` and submission growth `s`, acceptance requires `|s - r| <= max(1e-9 * max(|r|, |s|), 1e-11)`. The reference value is part of the denominator convention (the larger of the two magnitudes). This bound covers ordinary double-precision serialization and cross-solver variation, including the tiny (below ~5e-13 in magnitude) near-zero optima whose sign or exact zero-vs-noise value is solver-dependent; it does not license rounding to fewer significant digits, since genuine optimum differences between distinct knockout sets in this model are separated from that noise by several orders of magnitude. A growth value must not be clamped, sign-corrected or rounded to a coarser precision than that bound permits. An infeasible solve must be reported with an empty `growth` field, not zero.\n\n**Cross-file consistency.** The following relations between the submitted files are enforced with the same tolerance: each single-reaction set row of `double_reaction_deletions.csv` must agree with the corresponding row of `single_reaction_deletions.csv`; the `PFK` row of `pfk_knockout_optima.csv` must agree with the `PFK` row of `single_reaction_deletions.csv`; the `b1723` gene row of `pfk_knockout_optima.csv` must agree with the `b1723` row of `single_gene_deletions.csv`; the wild-type row must agree in growth with the `b1723` row of `single_gene_deletions.csv` (isozyme pfkB compensates pfkA removal); and the `b1723;b3916` row must agree with the `PFK` reaction-knockout rows (removing both PFK genes disables exactly the PFK reaction, which the supplied model's GPR associations define via `b1723` and `b3916` on PFK only).\n\nNo software stack is prescribed; any implementation producing these values is acceptable, and agreement of the alternative stacks used during validation is demonstrated, not assumed for others.",
  "grader_code": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Deterministic grader for E. coli core knockout FBA outputs.\n\nUsage:\n    python grade.py --reference-dir PATH --submission-dir PATH --report PATH\n\nCompares four CSV artifacts (knockouts,growth,status) row-by-row after keying\non the knockouts label. Populations are derived from the trusted task input\n(BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR/e_coli_core.xml), never from the submission.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport csv\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport xml.etree.ElementTree as ET\n\nFBC = \"{http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/fbc/version2}\"\nCORE = \"{http://www.sbml.org/sbml/level3/version1/core}\"\n\nGENE_FILE = \"single_gene_deletions.csv\"\nREACTION_FILE = \"single_reaction_deletions.csv\"\nDOUBLE_FILE = \"double_reaction_deletions.csv\"\nPFK_FILE = \"pfk_knockout_optima.csv\"\n\nPFK_LABELS = [\"\", \"PFK\", \"b1723\", \";\".join(sorted((\"b1723\", \"b3916\")))]\nHEADER = [\"knockouts\", \"growth\", \"status\"]\n\nREL_TOL = 1e-9\nABS_TOL = 1e-11\n\nALL_FILES = [DOUBLE_FILE, GENE_FILE, PFK_FILE, REACTION_FILE]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- table syntax\n\ndef _read_table(path):\n    \"\"\"Read a comma-delimited table; return (header, rows) or raise.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        from biotasks_table_io import read_delimited_table  # type: ignore\n    except ImportError:\n        read_delimited_table = None\n    if read_delimited_table is not None:\n        return read_delimited_table(path)\n    records = []\n    with open(path, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\") as stream:\n        for row in csv.reader(stream, delimiter=\",\", strict=True):\n            if not row:\n                raise ValueError(\"empty CSV record\")\n            records.append(row)\n    if not records:\n        raise ValueError(\"table has no header\")\n    header, rows = records[0], records[1:]\n    if any(len(row) != len(header) for row in rows):\n        raise ValueError(\"inconsistent row widths\")\n    return header, rows\n\n\ndef _load(path):\n    \"\"\"Return (table dict, None) or (None, error message).\"\"\"\n    if not os.path.isfile(path):\n        return None, \"file not found: %s\" % path\n    try:\n        header, rows = _read_table(path)\n    except Exception as exc:  # malformed syntax is a failed check, not a crash\n        return None, \"unreadable or malformed CSV (%s): %s\" % (path, exc)\n    if header != HEADER:\n        return None, \"header is %r, expected %r\" % (header, HEADER)\n    if len(set(header)) != len(header):\n        return None, \"duplicate header names\"\n    table = {}\n    for row in rows:\n        key = row[0]\n        if key in table:\n            return None, \"duplicate knockouts entry: %r\" % key\n        table[key] = (row[1], row[2])\n    return table, None\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------ model population\n\ndef _model_population(trusted_dir):\n    \"\"\"Gene and reaction id populations from the trusted SBML input.\"\"\"\n Knockout populations (137 genes, 95 reactions, 4560 pair/singleton sets, four PFK labels) are derived inside the grader from the trusted input `e_coli_core.xml` via `BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR` (SBML fbc:geneProduct labels; reaction ids with the `R_`/`G_` prefixes stripped, verified to match the model-aware parse: cobra reads the same file to 137 genes / 95 reactions / objective `Biomass_Ecoli_core`). No entity counts, ids or answer values are embedded; empty, missing, malformed, duplicate or nonfinite data fail the checks rather than crashing (exit 0 with a complete report in all cases; verified on an empty submission and on per-file missing cases, each producing the expected failures).\n\nTOLERANCE CALIBRATION (measured). Reference-vs-recomputed and reference-vs-independent-program differences, and within-reference gap structure, were measured before fixing bounds: (1) within the reference, near-duplicate optima (mathematically equal LP solutions across distinct knockout sets) are separated from genuine optimum differences by a large gap — the largest relative difference among near-duplicate optima is 3.90e-12 while the smallest genuine relative difference between distinct optima is 1.59e-6; (2) across three independently executed result sets, the maximum relative deviation on meaningful (|value| > 1e-6) optima is 3.91e-12; (3) on near-zero optima (|value| < 1e-6, up to 4.72e-13 in magnitude), sign flips and zero-vs-noise changes of up to 4.72e-13 absolute occur between correct runs. A relative tolerance of 1e-9 with an absolute floor of 1e-11 therefore accepts all demonstrated correct-run variation with ~20x margin on the noise side, yet rejects genuine differences (~1.6e-6 relative) by more than three orders of magnitude, rejects 4-decimal rounding, and rejects clamping or sign correction of meaningful values. The bound is a limit on observable output differences, not a guarantee that every wrong method is caught.\n\nSTATUS/EMPTY-FIELD SEMANTICS. In all reference files, a row's growth field is empty exactly when its status is not `optimal` (2/2/352/0 empty cells); the grader enforces exact status strings and empty-growth-iff-non-optimal, so an infeasible row reported as 0.0 fails.\n\nCROSS-FILE RELATIONS. Grounded in inspected model facts, not in the reference copy: the double-deletion singleton rows must equal the single-reaction rows (same LP); PFK-reaction rows across files must agree; the b1723 gene row must equal the wild-type growth within tolerance (PFK GPR is `b3916 or b1723`, and both b1723 and b3916 appear only in PFK, so pfkB compensates and the double gene knockout is exactly the PFK reaction knockout). These were verified to hold in the reference, the recomputed and the independent executions.\n\nVALIDATION EXECUTED. Reference self-comparison passes all nine checks; both independently executed result sets (recomputed oracle and the independently written program using multiprocess deletion runs and `repr` serialization) pass all nine checks with byte-different files — demonstrating that row order, float formatting and solver noise are correctly normalized. Negative controls executed and rejected: one double-deletion value perturbed by 1e-4 relative; 4-decimal rounding of gene growth (130 row failures); NaN injection; zero-clamping of tiny negative noise growth (detected as differences beyond the absolute floor); appended duplicate row; deleted pfk row; infeasible row restated as optimal with growth 0.0; files placed under an extra `outputs/` layer; empty submission; each file individually deleted (3 failing checks each). Grader runtime is under 0.1 s per execution.\n\nUNRESOLVED LIMITATIONS. The tolerance is calibrated on the demonstrated cobra/GLPK stack and the three available executions; broader cross-solver portability is not established (kept as public wording: demonstrated, not assumed). The `pfk_knockout_optima.csv` endpoint has no recorded baseline artifact from the original notebook run; it is validated against the independently recomputed oracle and an independently written program, which agree with the reference copy to the last digit, and is additionally constrained by the cross-file relations that do have recorded baselines. duplicated-row handling permits reordered rows by design, which is a stated public convention, not an oversight."

Required fields:

  • "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation

  • "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:

  • "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:

  • "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
  • "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:

  • You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
  • For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
    • C-c for Ctrl+C
    • C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:

  • Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
  • Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
  • Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
  • The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
  • Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:

Growth effects of gene and reaction knockouts in the E. coli core metabolic model

Objective

You are given the curated "textbook" E. coli core metabolic model (BiGG id e_coli_core) as an SBML file. Using flux balance analysis (FBA), determine how every possible single-gene deletion, every single-reaction deletion, every pairwise reaction deletion, and four specific knockout scenarios that illustrate gene-level redundancy for phosphofructokinase affect the maximal achievable growth.

By "growth" we mean the optimal value of the model's biomass objective (the raw LP objective value; no rounding, clamping or sign correction). For every knockout scenario, report that optimum together with the status reported by the LP solve (e.g. optimal or infeasible).

Supplied input

  • inputs/e_coli_core.xml — the E. coli core metabolic model in SBML format, including its biomass objective reaction and gene–protein–reaction (GPR) associations. Use the model exactly as supplied; do not modify it, its medium, bounds or objective.

Knockout semantics

  • Reaction knockout: the reaction carries no flux; its flux is constrained to zero in both directions.
  • Gene knockout: a reaction is disabled only if its GPR rule evaluates to false once the knocked-out gene(s) are removed. If a reaction has a remaining functional isozyme gene (an OR in the GPR), the reaction still carries flux; a gene whose removal disables no reaction therefore has no growth effect even though the gene is knocked out.

Required outputs

Produce four CSV files, all with the columns knockouts,growth,status:

  • knockouts: the identifier(s) of the knocked-out entity, exactly as defined in the supplied model. For a knockout of multiple entities, the ids are sorted lexicographically and joined with ; (e.g. b1723;b3916, Biomass_Ecoli_core;LDH_D); a single-entity knockout uses just that entity's id.
  • growth: the optimal objective value of the LP after the knockout, as reported by the solver at full double precision, with no rounding, clamping or sign correction. Tiny negative values of magnitude around 1e-14 that arise from solver noise are expected and must be reported as-is. Leave this field empty when the knockout makes the problem infeasible.
  • status: the LP solve status string, e.g. optimal or infeasible.

1. single_gene_deletions.csv

One row for every gene defined in the supplied model (137 genes), including genes whose deletion disables no reaction.

2. single_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for every reaction defined in the supplied model (95 reactions, including boundary/exchange reactions).

3. double_reaction_deletions.csv

One row for each distinct knockout set {r_i, r_j} obtained by pairing every reaction in the model with every reaction in the model and reducing each ordered pair to an unordered set; the i = j cases contribute the single-reaction sets {r_i}. This yields the 95 singleton sets plus all C(95,2) = 4465 pairs, i.e. 4560 rows. Do not apply gene-level GPR logic here — both reactions are knocked out directly.

4. pfk_knockout_optima.csv

Exactly four rows, with the same column convention and an empty knockouts field for the no-knockout row:

  • (empty) — the unmodified (wild-type) model, no knockout;
  • PFK — the PFK reaction knocked out;
  • b1723 — gene b1723 (pfkA) knocked out;
  • b1723;b3916 — genes b1723 (pfkA) and b3916 (pfkB) knocked out simultaneously.

These quantify isozyme redundancy: the isozyme pfkB can compensate for a pfkA deletion, but not when both genes are removed.

Conventions

  • Row order in every file carries no scientific meaning; any row ordering is acceptable.
  • Growth is reported in the model's native biomass-objective units (the raw LP objective value).
  • Use the knockout populations exactly as defined above; do not skip entities that have no reaction associations or no growth effect.
  • Do not round any value (growth is written at full double precision).

Environment and resources

CPU only (up to 4 cores), 8 GiB RAM, no network access. Your program must complete within 600 seconds. Any software stack that satisfies the definitions above is acceptable; the results, not the tool, are what is compared.

Exact acceptance criteria (including numerical tolerances appropriate for LP-solver variation) are finalized separately during validation before the contract takes effect; produce results faithful to the definitions above.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules for the knockout-FBA outputs

Files compared. Exactly the four declared output files, each read as a comma-delimited UTF-8 CSV at its declared path relative to the supplied output root (no fallback directories, no extra outputs/ layer): single_gene_deletions.csv, single_reaction_deletions.csv, double_reaction_deletions.csv, pfk_knockout_optima.csv.

CSV syntax. Each file must carry exactly the header knockouts,growth,status and every data row must have exactly three fields (quoted empty fields and decimal values following standard CSV quoting are ordinary data; blank records are not permitted). Values must be plain decimal numbers in a standard fixed or scientific notation; hexadecimal, inf, nan or other nonfinite/invalid numerics fail. The growth field must be empty exactly when the solve is not optimal; for optimal rows it must contain a finite number.

Row alignment and ordering. Comparison is by the knockouts key, not by file position: any row order is acceptable. Each knockout label must appear exactly once; duplicate labels fail. Labels for multi-entity knockouts are the lexicographically sorted ids joined with ;; single-entity knockouts use the bare id. The empty wild-type row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv uses an empty knockouts field.

Coverage (input-grounded). The knockout population is derived from the supplied model e_coli_core.xml, not from the reference file: single_gene_deletions.csv must contain exactly one row per gene defined in the model; single_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per reaction defined in the model (including boundary/exchange reactions); double_reaction_deletions.csv exactly one row per single-reaction set and per unordered reaction pair (the 95 singletons plus all C(95,2) pairs, i.e. 4560 rows); pfk_knockout_optima.csv exactly the four rows "", PFK, b1723, b1723;b3916. Missing rows, extra rows or a different population fail.

Status comparison. The status string is compared exactly (e.g. optimal, infeasible); any status text that differs from the reference status for that knockout fails.

Numeric comparison. For each row with reference growth r and submission growth s, acceptance requires |s - r| <= max(1e-9 * max(|r|, |s|), 1e-11). The reference value is part of the denominator convention (the larger of the two magnitudes). This bound covers ordinary double-precision serialization and cross-solver variation, including the tiny (below ~5e-13 in magnitude) near-zero optima whose sign or exact zero-vs-noise value is solver-dependent; it does not license rounding to fewer significant digits, since genuine optimum differences between distinct knockout sets in this model are separated from that noise by several orders of magnitude. A growth value must not be clamped, sign-corrected or rounded to a coarser precision than that bound permits. An infeasible solve must be reported with an empty growth field, not zero.

Cross-file consistency. The following relations between the submitted files are enforced with the same tolerance: each single-reaction set row of double_reaction_deletions.csv must agree with the corresponding row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the PFK row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the PFK row of single_reaction_deletions.csv; the b1723 gene row of pfk_knockout_optima.csv must agree with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv; the wild-type row must agree in growth with the b1723 row of single_gene_deletions.csv (isozyme pfkB compensates pfkA removal); and the b1723;b3916 row must agree with the PFK reaction-knockout rows (removing both PFK genes disables exactly the PFK reaction, which the supplied model's GPR associations define via b1723 and b3916 on PFK only).

No software stack is prescribed; any implementation producing these values is acceptable, and agreement of the alternative stacks used during validation is demonstrated, not assumed for others.

Task directories

Read the supplied inputs from /workspace/inputs/. Write all required output files under /workspace/outputs/, using the relative filenames specified above. The working directory is /workspace. Aliases /inputs/ and /outputs/ refer to these same directories.

"""Operator release staging from accepted native evidence; never edits task science."""

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from release_metadata import (
    additional_release_evidence,
    load_release_metadata,
    release_execution_provenance,
    scientific_probe_documents,
    verify_bundle_licenses,
)
from repo2rlenv.campaigns.release import ReleasePlan, ReleaseTask, stage_release, verify_release
from repo2rlenv.emitter.evaluation import EvaluationLabel, evaluation_time
from repo2rlenv.quality.labels import write_labeled_copy

config_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
config = json.loads(config_path.read_text())
metadata, licenses, provenance = load_release_metadata(config)
native, task, grading, stage = map(
    Path, [config[k] for k in ("native", "task", "grading", "stage")]
)
assert not stage.exists()
checked = subprocess.run(
    [
        sys.executable,
        str(Path(__file__).with_name("check_scientific_release.py")),
        str(native),
        str(task),
        str(grading),
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=True,
)
validation = json.loads(checked.stdout)
assert validation["accepted"] is True
verify_bundle_licenses(task, licenses)
execution_provenance, execution_documents = release_execution_provenance(config, validation)


def read(path):
    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())


# Upstream's verified label specifically requires its standard quality-loop proof.
# Preserve that distinction rather than fabricating compatible trial records.
labeled = write_labeled_copy(
    task,
    Path(config["labeled"]) / task.name,
    EvaluationLabel(
        status="unverified",
        stage="complete",
        provenance=execution_provenance,
        reason_codes=["upstream_quality_loop_not_run"],
        checked_at=evaluation_time(),
        profile="biotasks-scientific-content-v1",
        subject_bundle_hash=validation["bundle_hash"],
        detail="BioTasks scientific-content controls and native Harbor controls passed; a blind GLM attempt was recorded. These checks use the BioTasks artifact workflow, not the standard upstream quality-loop acceptance profile. See the release validation evidence.",
    ),
)
raw_summary = read(native / "result.json")
trajectory = native / raw_summary["solver"]["result_path"]
trajectory = trajectory.parent / "agent/trajectory.json"
assert trajectory.is_file()
documents = {
    **execution_documents,
    "validation-summary.json": validation,
    "grading-result.json": read(grading / "result.json"),
    "grading-controls.json": {"controls": read(grading / "final-controls.json")},
    "grading-rationale.json": {"rationale": read(grading / "final-candidate.json")["rationale"]},
    "grading-review.json": read(
        grading
        / ("review-repair.json" if (grading / "review-repair.json").exists() else "review.json")
    ),
    "independent-solution.json": read(grading / "independent-solution.json"),
    "independent-execution.json": read(grading / "independent-result.json"),
    **scientific_probe_documents(grading),
    "solver-trajectory.json": read(trajectory),
    "source-licenses.json": licenses,
    "source-intake-provenance.json": provenance,
    "materialization-manifest.json": read(Path(config["materialization"]) / "manifest.json"),
    "materialization-rationale.json": {
        "rationale": read(Path(config["materialization"]) / "candidate.json")["rationale"]
    },
}
documents.update(additional_release_evidence(config, reserved=documents))
plan = ReleasePlan(
    repo_id=metadata["repo_id"],
    recipe="notebook-artifact-reproduction",
    title=metadata["title"],
    description=metadata["description"],
    methodology=metadata["methodology"],
    code_revision=config["revision"],
    tasks=[
        ReleaseTask(
            path=labeled,
            bundle_hash=validation["bundle_hash"],
            evidence={
                "scientific_content_controls_passed": True,
                "native_trials": validation["native_trials"],
                "standard_upstream_quality_loop_run": False,
            },
            evidence_documents=documents,
        )
    ],
    economics={
        "model": "glm-5.3",
        "solver_seconds_limit": 600,
        "cpu": 4,
        "memory_gib": 8,
        "disk_gib": 10,
        "actual_daytona_invoice_usd": None,
        "aggregate_authorized_usd": config.get("aggregate_authorized_usd", "100.00"),
    },
    citations=metadata["citations"],
    limitations=[
        "One task and one final blind attempt do not establish benchmark performance or universal software portability.",
        "The upstream advisory evaluation label remains unverified because its standard quality-loop profile was not run. The separate, executed BioTasks scientific-content and native-control evidence is provided explicitly.",
        "All authoring, validation implementation and solver workers used GLM-5.3; separation of inputs does not imply independence of model families.",
        "The frozen reference and inputs ground this computational reproduction task; successful execution and numerical agreement do not establish biological validity.",
        "The Python dependency lock is preserved. Base-image tags and system-package repositories are not immutable rebuild guarantees.",
        "The source notebook and reference-derived answers are public, so this is not a hidden contamination-free benchmark.",
    ],
)
plan_path = Path(config["plan"])
plan_path.write_text(plan.model_dump_json(indent=2) + "\n")
manifest = stage_release(plan, stage)
verify_release(stage)
print(
    json.dumps(
        {
            "staged": str(stage),
            "bundle_hash": validation["bundle_hash"],
            "task_count": manifest["task_count"],
            "plan": str(plan_path),
        }
    )
)
Final recorded-review gate

repo:experiments/19-repo2rlenv-notebook-pilot/release_review.py

"""Recheck the final recorded review without new model or scientific execution."""

import json
import time

from grading_protocol import (
    Grader,
    Review,
    check_review_asset_hints,
    check_review_scientific_admission,
    check_review_source_coverage,
)
from probe_coverage import unexercised_scientific_checks


def recorded_review_context(grading, inputs):
    if "review_evidence" not in inputs:
        return inputs
    from review_packet import ReviewPacket

    packet = ReviewPacket.open_recorded(
        grading / "review-inspection/review-packets",
        inputs["review_evidence"],
        deadline=time.time() + 60,
    )
    original = packet.reconstruct()
    inline = {key: value for key, value in inputs.items() if key != "review_evidence"}
    if inline != {
        key: value for key, value in original.items() if key in ReviewPacket.INLINE_FIELDS
    }:
        raise ValueError("Inline review inputs differ from their recorded packet")
    return original


def check_final_review(grading):
    def read(path):
        return json.loads(path.read_text())

    candidate = read(grading / "final-candidate.json")
    review = Review.model_validate(
        read(
            grading
            / ("review-repair.json" if (grading / "review-repair.json").exists() else "review.json")
        )
    )
    if review.decision != "accept_for_packaging" or review.issues:
        raise ValueError("Release requires an accepting final review without issues")
    check_review_source_coverage(review)
    # A repair worker may have several submission reviews. Bind the final review
    # to its recorded response and exact candidate, not to the first input file.
    matched = []
    for path in grading.glob("review*/input.json"):
        artifact = path.parent / "artifact-stage/artifact.json"
        if not artifact.is_file():
            continue
        observed = Review.model_validate(read(artifact)["artifact"])
        if observed == review:
            inputs = recorded_review_context(grading, read(path))
            if inputs["candidate"] == candidate:
                matched.append(inputs)
    if not matched:
        raise ValueError("Final review is not bound to a recorded input and exact candidate")
    for inputs in matched:
        check_review_scientific_admission(review, inputs["artifact_interface"]["output_paths"])
        check_review_asset_hints(review, inputs["asset_value_hints"]["findings"])
    controls = read(grading / "final-controls.json")
    if unexercised_scientific_checks(Grader.model_validate(candidate), controls):
        raise ValueError("Every scientific check needs an executed scientific negative")
    return review

"""Verify a pinned upstream release after downloading its mode-preserving archive."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import tarfile
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

from repo2rlenv.campaigns.release import verify_release
from repo2rlenv.emitter.bundle import inspect_bundle

MAX_FILE_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS = 4096
MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 16384
MAX_PATH_BYTES = 1024


def safe_path(name: str) -> Path:
    if not name or len(name.encode()) > MAX_PATH_BYTES or "\\" in name or "\x00" in name:
        raise ValueError("Unsafe release path")
    value = PurePosixPath(name)
    if value.is_absolute() or ".." in value.parts or value.as_posix() != name:
        raise ValueError("Unsafe release path")
    return Path(name)


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    result = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        while chunk := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
            result.update(chunk)
    return result.hexdigest()


def bounded_archive(source, destination, entries):
    """Bound raw headers before tarfile parses extended metadata; validate before extracting."""
    expected_files = {name for name in entries if name.startswith("tasks/")}
    expected_dirs = {
        parent.as_posix()
        for name in expected_files
        for parent in Path(name).parents
        if parent != Path(".")
    }
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as raw:
        with gzip.open(source, "rb") as compressed:
            total = 0
            for index in range(MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS + 1):
                header = compressed.read(512)
                if header == b"\0" * 512:
                    raw.write(header)
                    break
                if len(header) != 512 or index == MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS:
                    raise ValueError("Invalid or excessive archive headers")
                member = tarfile.TarInfo.frombuf(header, "utf-8", "surrogateescape")
                if member.size < 0 or member.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES:
                    raise ValueError("Archive member exceeds size bound")
                if (
                    member.type
                    in {
                        tarfile.XHDTYPE,
                        tarfile.XGLTYPE,
                        tarfile.GNUTYPE_LONGNAME,
                        tarfile.GNUTYPE_LONGLINK,
                    }
                    and member.size > MAX_METADATA_BYTES
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Archive metadata exceeds bound")
                size = (member.size + 511) // 512 * 512
                total += 512 + size
                if total > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES + 8 * 1024 * 1024:
                    raise ValueError("Archive expansion exceeds bound")
                raw.write(header)
                while size:
                    block = compressed.read(min(size, 65536))
                    if not block:
                        raise ValueError("Truncated archive")
                    raw.write(block)
                    size -= len(block)
        seen = set()
        raw.seek(0)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="r|") as archive:
            for member in archive:
                if member.name in seen or len(seen) >= MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS:
                    raise ValueError("Duplicate or excessive archive entries")
                seen.add(member.name)
                safe_path(member.name)
                if member.isdir():
                    if member.name not in expected_dirs:
                        raise ValueError("Unexpected archive directory")
                elif member.isfile() and not member.sparse:
                    entry = entries.get(member.name)
                    if (
                        member.name not in expected_files
                        or member.size != entry["bytes"]
                        or member.mode != entry["mode"]
                    ):
                        raise ValueError("Archive differs from release manifest")
                else:
                    raise ValueError("Archive must contain regular files and directories")
        if not expected_files.issubset(seen):
            raise ValueError("Missing archive files")
        raw.seek(0)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="r|") as archive:
            for member in archive:
                if member.isfile():
                    target = destination / safe_path(member.name)
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with archive.extractfile(member) as src, target.open("xb") as dst:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, length=65536)
                    target.chmod(member.mode)


def check_download(repo_id: str, revision: str, destination: Path, download) -> dict:
    """Download only public release files, restore modes, then call upstream checks.

    ``download(name)`` must fetch from the explicit immutable publication revision.
    A new destination prevents cached local task files from satisfying the check.
    """
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", revision):
        raise ValueError("Use the immutable publication commit")
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    manifest_source = Path(download("release-files.json"))
    if manifest_source.stat().st_size > 1024 * 1024:
        raise ValueError("Release manifest is too large")
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_source.read_text())
    if manifest["repo_id"] != repo_id:
        raise ValueError("Downloaded release belongs to a different repository")
    entries = manifest["files"]
    if sum(v["bytes"] for v in entries.values()) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        raise ValueError("Release exceeds the bounded local download allowance")
    for name, entry in entries.items():
        safe_path(name)
        if not 0 <= entry["bytes"] <= MAX_FILE_BYTES or not 0 <= entry["mode"] <= 0o777:
            raise ValueError("Invalid release size or mode")
    shutil.copyfile(manifest_source, destination / "release-files.json")
    for name, entry in entries.items():
        if name.startswith("tasks/"):
            continue
        source = Path(download(name))
        if source.stat().st_size != entry["bytes"] or digest(source) != entry["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError(f"Downloaded bytes changed: {name}")
        target = destination / safe_path(name)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(source, target)
        target.chmod(entry["mode"])
    bounded_archive(destination / "tasks.tar.gz", destination, entries)
    verify_release(destination)
    release = json.loads((destination / "manifest.json").read_text())
    bundles = []
    for row in release["tasks"]:
        identity = inspect_bundle(destination / safe_path(row["path"]))
        if not identity["integrity_passed"] or identity["bundle_hash"] != row["bundle_hash"]:
            raise ValueError("Downloaded task identity changed")
        bundles.append({"task_id": row["task_id"], "bundle_hash": identity["bundle_hash"]})
    return {"repo_id": repo_id, "revision": revision, "verified": True, "tasks": bundles}


def main():
    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("repo_id")
    parser.add_argument("revision")
    parser.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--receipt", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = check_download(
        args.repo_id,
        args.revision,
        args.destination,
        lambda name: hf_hub_download(
            args.repo_id, name, repo_type="dataset", revision=args.revision, force_download=True
        ),
    )
    args.receipt.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(result))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
